target_customer: Multi-site retail and restaurant chains managing repairs and maintenance
problem: Chains struggle to coordinate repair requests and contractors across many locations.
business_model: B2B SaaS (marketplace structure, no take rate)
product_category: Commercial maintenance and work order software

founders.name: Matt Velker
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder and head of product on YC, CEO on Sacra.

technical_complexity.rationale: Work order routing, contractor onboarding and payments are standard SaaS engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Embedded in customer workflows and contractor network, but larger platforms do similar work.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: ServiceChannel was acquired by Fortive for about 1.2 billion dollars per Sacra; OpenWrench remained independent with an estimated 1.7M USD 2024 revenue (Latka estimate).

market_need_then: Multi-location brands outsource repairs and rely on large incumbents; a Capterra review describes a customer coordinating emergency maintenance across 30 plus locations.

branding.domain_note: Uses useopenwrench.com, a prefixed domain, suggesting openwrench.com was not obtained; no source states this.

brand_strength.rationale: Name is confused in search with Wrench, an unrelated Seattle auto-repair company; otherwise a modest B2B brand.

outcome_analysis: OpenWrench appears to be a small, capital-efficient B2B SaaS business that has operated for years since Summer 2018 with a reported tiny outside raise and revenue estimated in the low millions. It has neither exited nor shut down; growth is constrained by a large incumbent and a fragmented market.
notes: CB Insights lists 150K USD convertible note Jan 2018 with YC; Latka says bootstrapped; single aggregator so not recorded as a round. Revenue figures are Latka estimates. No dated 2018 competitor sources found. Outcome search found no events. Completeness pass: Convertible note rests on CB Insights (Sacra also lists 150K); Latka says bootstrapped, a conflict.
